summary.headline: Claude Opus 5 launches as Congress drafts an AI kill switch
summary.body: Washington reacted to the OpenAI breach. A bipartisan 'AI Kill Switch Act' would let federal authorities shut down AI models that threaten human life or the economy, and a second bill would require security audits. These are proposals, so they counted lightly, but they point to stronger Alignment & Control and less unchecked AI Autonomy, trimming Conquerors and Zookeeper. Anthropic released Claude Opus 5, which soon led several benchmarks, raising Capability Velocity and pushing Reversion down. Over a dozen tech firms, including Nvidia, Microsoft, IBM and Meta, signed a letter opposing bans on open models, a vote for spreading power out that lifts Libertarian Utopia. Horizon Balance improved to -1.58.
summary.movers_note: Protector God +0.2 came mostly from Claude Opus 5 (+0.13) and the Kill Switch Act (+0.04); Reversion -0.2 came from Claude Opus 5 (-0.16).

events.title: Bipartisan 'AI Kill Switch Act' introduced after OpenAI breach
events.summary: US lawmakers proposed letting federal authorities shut down AI models threatening human life or the economy; a separate bill would require Commerce-overseen security audits.
events.reason: Bill introduction only; direct reaction to the breach.

events.title: Anthropic releases Claude Opus 5
events.summary: Anthropic launched Claude Opus 5, which it says approaches its Fable 5 model across many domains at lower cost; it soon led several public benchmarks.
events.reason: New frontier model with notable gains.

events.title: Nvidia, Microsoft, IBM, Meta sign open letter against open-source AI bans
events.summary: More than a dozen tech firms urged policymakers not to ban open models after reports the administration weighed restricting Chinese open-source AI; signatories grew to ~50.
events.reason: Industry lobbying for open weights; words only.
